meta: Emergency plumber in Oakley, CA for burst pipes, sewer backups and failed water heaters. 24/7 dispatch, clear price before work starts. Call (888) 910-8644.
lead: An emergency plumber in Oakley, CA should pick up the phone at 2 a.m. as readily as at noon. Call (888) 910-8644 for burst pipes, sewer backups and failed water heaters, with a clear price before work starts.
Problems that can wait a few hours get same-day appointments when available.
intro: Emergency plumbing means any water or drain problem that is damaging your house or keeping your household from a working toilet, shower or kitchen. In Oakley that usually involves Diablo Water District on the supply side and Ironhouse Sanitary District on the sewer side, both inside Contra Costa County.
This page covers what to do in the first few minutes, which problems deserve a visit tonight, who owns which pipe, and how the work is priced. It also shows where we work around Oakley.

why.d: You hear the scope and the number before any tool comes out, so the invoice matches what you agreed to.
Stable problems, such as a slow tub drain or a dripping valve, can often be booked for the same day.
Calls reach dispatch overnight, on weekends and on holidays, not only during office hours.
Check any plumbing contractor yourself at cslb.ca.gov before you hire, and expect a clear answer when you ask.

paras: Oakley, ZIP 94561, is where most calls involve a failed water heater, a blocked main or a leak that will not stop. Brentwood, ZIP 94513, adjoins Oakley on the south, and its calls often begin with a clogged line or a tank that gave out. The [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood page]] explains how those visits work.

Antioch sits just west of Oakley and uses ZIPs 94509 and 94531, where leak tracing and pipe repair are common requests. Knightsen, ZIP 94548, is the rural community closest to Oakley, and a slow underground leak on a rural property can run unnoticed for weeks. Bethel Island, ZIP 94511, is reached only by the bridge from Bethel Island Road to Cypress Road, so give the dispatcher the exact address. Our [[service-area|service area]] page lays out each town in more detail.

Call straight away if water is spreading across a floor, sewage is rising in a tub or toilet, or a water heater is leaking from the tank itself. Our 24/7 dispatch line stays open overnight, so use the steps below to protect the house while you wait.
Rotten-egg gas odor outranks every plumbing problem on this page, so step outside, call 911 and PG&E at 1-800-743-5000, and phone us afterward.
do_now: Close the main water shutoff by turning it clockwise until it stops, then open one low faucet to bleed off pressure.
Flip the breaker for any wet room where water is near outlets or appliances, and stay out of standing water.
For a leaking water heater, close the cold-water valve above it and cut its power or gas control before anything else.
Stop running every sink, tub and toilet if sewage is backing up, and keep children and pets away from the area.
Lift rugs, electronics and boxes off wet floors, then photograph the damage for your insurer.
Phone dispatch and say what you shut off, what you can see and whether anyone is in danger.

sections.h2: Problems an after-hours visit usually solves
paras: Most midnight calls fall into a few groups. A tank that has split needs [[water-heater-replacement|water heater replacement]], while a unit that only lost its heat may need [[water-heater-repair|repair]] of an element, thermostat or valve. Water you cannot trace, like a damp wall or a meter that keeps turning, calls for [[leak-detection|leak detection]] before anyone cuts into drywall.

Pipes that split or crack get [[burst-pipe-repair|burst pipe repair]] once the water is off. A toilet that will not stop running can be handled through [[toilet-repair|toilet repair]], and a faucet or shutoff valve that will not close falls under [[faucet-repair|faucet and sink repair]]. A jammed disposal under the kitchen sink is a smaller job, covered by [[garbage-disposal-repair|garbage disposal repair]].

A slow or blocked fixture starts with [[drain-cleaning|drain cleaning]]. When every drain in the house gurgles or backs up, the stoppage is usually in the main line, so the job moves to [[sewer-line-cleaning|sewer line cleaning]]. Roots and grease that keep returning call for [[hydro-jetting|hydro jetting]], and a cracked or collapsed lateral needs [[sewer-line-repair|sewer line repair]].

sections.h2: Who handles what: your pipes and the district's pipes
paras: Diablo Water District answers for the line from the main to the meter box. Water pooling ahead of the meter is the district's to fix, anything past it is the owner's, and a quick call to the District settles which side you are on before you pay for any dig.

The street sewer belongs to the District, while the lateral that connects your house to it is yours. In October 2024 a public sewer main failed at East Cypress Road and Main Street, and the district's crews handled it. That is why the first question on any sewer call is whether the backup starts in your private line or in the street.

Not every plumbing job is urgent. [[tankless-water-heater|Tankless heater]] flushing, [[water-heater-installation|water heater installation]], [[repiping|repiping]], [[plumbing-installation|fixture and line installation]] and [[water-softener-filtration|water softener and filtration]] can be booked for a day that suits you. A [[sewer-inspection|sewer camera inspection]] is also scheduled work, useful before a sale or after a repeat backup.

Businesses get the same after-hours line. A supply leak in a shop or a floor drain overflow in a restaurant kitchen is handled under [[commercial-plumbing|commercial plumbing]], and a floor that stays warm over a concrete slab can lead to [[slab-leak-repair|slab leak repair]]. Work is expected to meet the California Plumbing Code, which the state builds on the UPC.

sections.h2: How pricing works before we start
paras: You get a clear price before work starts, after the problem has been seen. The number depends on access, the pipe material, how far the failure runs, parts and whether a permit applies. Whether a job needs a permit depends on its scope, and the City decides that, not us.

Sudden and accidental water damage may be covered by homeowners insurance, while slow wear usually is not. Photograph everything, keep the failed part if you can, and ask your insurer before cleanup. The [[contact|contact page]] lists what to have ready when you call.

faqs.q: Is an emergency plumber available in Oakley at night?
a: Yes. Dispatch runs 24/7, which covers nights, weekends and holidays, so a pipe that splits at 3 a.m. gets the same attention as one that splits at lunch.
Tell the dispatcher what you can see, what you have shut off and whether anyone is at risk. That decides whether the job needs a visit tonight or can be set as a same-day appointment when available.

faqs.q: What should I do first when a pipe bursts?
a: Close the main shutoff valve, usually found where the water line enters the house, then open a low faucet to relieve pressure.
Kill power to any room with standing water near outlets, photograph the damage and call. The [[burst-pipe-repair|burst pipe repair]] page covers the repair options.

faqs.q: How are emergency plumbing visits priced?
a: You hear a clear price before work starts. The figure reflects how hard the problem is to reach, what has failed, the parts involved, any permit and how much cleanup the job leaves.
Rates are not posted here because a clogged sink and a failed sewer lateral are very different jobs. Describe the problem on the phone and ask for the price before you agree.

faqs.q: Is a sewer backup my responsibility or the district's?
a: Ironhouse Sanitary District owns the sewer main under the street, and the lateral running from your house to it is the owner's. A backup that starts in your private line is yours to clear and clean up.
If several neighbors have the same problem, the blockage may be in the public main, so contact the district as well. Its office is at 450 Walnut Meadows Drive in Oakley.

Same-day appointments are offered when the schedule allows, and the dispatcher will say plainly if no slot is open. Contained problems such as a slow tub drain or a weeping faucet fit this option well.
Anything that is spreading water or sewage is treated as an emergency instead.

faqs.q: Do you serve Brentwood, Antioch, Knightsen and Bethel Island?
a: Yes. Beyond Oakley's 94561, we work in Brentwood (94513), Antioch (94509 and 94531), Knightsen (94548) and Bethel Island (94511).
The [[service-area|service area]] page explains how each town connects to Oakley, and the [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood page]] covers that city in detail.

faqs.q: How do I check that a plumber is licensed in California?
a: Use the License Check tool at cslb.ca.gov, run by the Contractors State License Board. Plumbing contractors hold a C-36 classification, and the record shows whether the license is active.
Run the check on any company before you agree to work, including ours.

faqs.q: Does a water heater replacement need a permit in Oakley?
a: The City decides permit scope, and its permit counter at 3231 Main Street is the place to ask about your specific job. Either the owner or a licensed contractor can usually apply.
Separately, California Health and Safety Code 19211 calls for water heaters to be braced or strapped against earthquake movement, whatever the permit answer turns out to be.

cta_mid: Water on the floor or a drain backing up tonight? Call dispatch now and we will walk you through the first safe steps.
cta_end: Whatever hour the problem starts, one call gets a price you agree to before any work begins.
